About

SkiScanner ranks every ski area in the world for our dates and group, with the crowds to expect, from openly available data. Nothing is invented: prices only where an official source exists.
How it ranks. "Your match" starts from piste km, top altitude (higher is usually snow-surer) and, where computed, the share of the last 10 winters with good snow in your weeks (historical, modelled from ERA5 reanalysis; not a forecast). The priorities you pick then carry two thirds of the weight: snow-sure (snow history, or altitude when none is computed), quiet slopes (predicted crowds in your week), big ski area (piste km), gentle (easy km and their share), steep (black km), easy to reach (distance to a large airport). A resort without the figure a priority needs is scored low for it and says so in its reasons. Resorts whose season doesn't cover your dates are left out. The other sorts use what OpenStreetMap mappers recorded for each area: piste km by colour (easy = blue/green, intermediate = red, advanced = black, freeride and expert), lifts by type (high-capacity = gondolas, cable cars, chairlifts, funiculars; the rest are drag lifts), top and base altitude, cross-country trails. Airports come from OurAirports (public domain): straight-line distance to the nearest airport with scheduled flights and to the nearest large airport, never driving time.
Which way the pistes face. The aspect rose on each card is computed from OpenSkiMap's run geometry (every downhill segment adds its length to the compass direction from its higher to its lower end), after the idea of OpenSkiStats. Slopes facing away from the midwinter sun (north in the northern hemisphere, south in the southern) hold snow longer; the yellow band shows where that sun stands from sunrise to sunset at the resort's latitude. "Shady slopes" is the share of piste length in the five compass sectors around that pole side.
Group session. One link carries the whole search (dates, group, priorities, sort, the compared resorts), so everyone sees the same options. With the group store connected the search also travels live between members who have the page open, and the session has its own comments; without it, share the link again after a change.
Not in any open dataset, so not shown rather than guessed: ski-in/ski-out, hotel and bed capacity, après-ski, spa and childcare, lift queues. Add what you know as a note on the resort's card.
Crowds. Nobody publishes how many people are at a resort, and Google's visit data forbids automated use, so the busyness shown is predicted from the official school and public holiday calendars of the main skiing countries (the season strip marks your weeks; "quieter" means no major holiday in those markets). Loaded: France, Germany (all states), England, the Netherlands, the US, Japan, Lunar New Year, New Zealand and Australia (NSW). Not loaded yet: .
Prices. Lift-pass totals use official tariffs read from the resorts' own pages (retrieval date shown); children use the age-10 tariff, and under-6s are often free, so check. Accommodation and flights open on the booking sites with your dates; SkiScanner shows no prices from them.
Budget. "Budget pp per day, all in" is divided into what is known per person per day: the official lift pass, and the figures the group enters on a card (the stay for the whole group, a car or transfers, lift passes where no official price exists, food and extras). Shared costs are split by the number of people, so the same chalet or car costs less per head in a bigger group. What is left after the known parts caps the stay links (Booking.com and Airbnb open with that maximum per night where they support it). Resorts over budget are marked and never hidden; the "ways to get there" under each budget are computed from real figures only: fewer ski days from the official tariff, a cheaper priced resort nearby, more people on the shared costs, or the gap to close. Entered figures are labelled as such and stay on your device (and in a session link, or in the group store when it is connected).
Getting there. Pick where you fly from and the page lists the gateway airports with the most pistes within 150 km of them, each with a one-tap fare check for your dates (Google Flights, Skyscanner) and a place to record the fare the group saw, per person return. SkiScanner fetches no fares: flight sites forbid automated reading and publish no open data, so the only fares on the page are the ones you enter, labelled with who entered them, when and for which dates. Resorts within 150 km of an airport with a recorded fare carry it into their budget line and into the "Cheapest flights found" sort; "Closest to home" is the straight line home → gateway → resort, never flight or driving time. From the airport on, the links open driving, public-transport and car-hire searches on Google Maps; transfer prices are not collected either.
Live info. Snow reports, lifts open and webcams are on each resort's own site (link on every card). "Piste map" opens OpenSkiMap on that resort; "Webcams" opens Windy's webcam map at the resort's coordinates (Windy does not document that link format, so zoom out if it lands off-centre).
Your choices stay on your device. The priorities, dates and group you enter are remembered in this browser only; nothing is sent anywhere unless you vote or write a note.
Votes and notes. "I'd go here", notes and messages are stored for the person who shared this page, with a random id for your device so a second tap removes your vote. No account, no tracking; your name is only what you type. The vote counts are shared with everyone who has the link; names and messages are not.
Sources.
    Data: OpenSkiMap / OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), Open-Meteo (CC-BY 4.0), Natural Earth, OurAirports (public domain), resorts' official price pages. Type: Fraunces, Barlow, IBM Plex Mono, Heebo, Frank Ruhl Libre (SIL Open Font License).
